name: Pituitary Hormone Deficiency Secondary to Storage Disease
aliases: Secondary Hypopituitarism due to Storage Disorder

criteria.description: Evidence of deficiency in one or more anterior pituitary hormones confirmed by biochemical testing
Confirmed diagnosis of an underlying lysosomal or other storage disease by enzymatic, genetic, or histopathological methods
MRI evidence of pituitary gland or stalk abnormalities consistent with infiltration or damage secondary to storage material accumulation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pituitary hormone deficiency plus confirmed underlying storage disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of primary pituitary disorders and other causes of hypopituitarism.

laboratory: Low serum levels of pituitary-dependent hormones (GH, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, prolactin)
Low target gland hormones (cortisol, free T4, sex steroids)
Enzymatic or genetic confirmation of storage disease
imaging: MRI showing pituitary gland hypoplasia, stalk thickening, or infiltration
Possible sellar or suprasellar mass lesions consistent with storage material accumulation
genetic: Mutations associated with specific storage diseases (e.g., lysosomal storage disorders)
other: Histopathological evidence of storage material accumulation in pituitary tissue (if biopsy performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Primary pituitary gland pathology without systemic storage disorder
Acute onset with hemorrhage or infarction of pituitary
Sudden headache and visual loss, unlike gradual progression in storage disease
Infiltration by sarcoidosis, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, or lymphoma
Different systemic features and biopsy findings

redFlags: Unexplained hypoglycemia in a patient with known storage disease
